subject: Business
title: Financial Independence: The FIRE Movement
description: One-minute skill: Financial Independence: The FIRE Movement.

hook.text: A 32-year-old software engineer retires with $1.2 million. Not because she's rich — because she needs less.

buildup.text: FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early) means saving aggressively so investment income covers living expenses.

discovery.text: The 4% rule: if annual expenses are 4% or less of your portfolio, you can withdraw indefinitely without running out.

twist.text: FIRE isn't about deprivation. It's about aligning spending with values and rejecting mindless consumption.

climax.text: With $1M invested and $40K annual expenses, you never need to work for money again. The math is simple.

punchline.text: Financial independence isn't about never working. It's about choosing why you work.

quiz.question: What is the 4% rule in the FIRE movement?
options: You can withdraw 4% of your portfolio annually without running out of money
You should save 4% of your income each month
Investment returns must exceed 4% to retire

details.summary: The FIRE movement pursues financial independence and early retirement by saving 50 to 70 percent of income and investing aggressively. The goal is accumulating enough investments that passive income covers all living expenses, making traditional employment optional.
details.whyItMatters: FIRE challenges the assumption that people must work until 65. Even if early retirement is not your goal, FIRE principles of high savings rates and intentional spending provide a powerful framework for financial freedom.
takeaways: FIRE targets saving 50 to 70 percent of income for early financial independence
The 4 percent rule estimates how much you need to withdraw sustainably
Variations include lean FIRE, fat FIRE, and barista FIRE for different lifestyles

faq.question: What is the 4 percent rule and is it reliable?
faq.answer: The Trinity Study found that withdrawing 4 percent of a stock and bond portfolio annually survived most 30-year historical periods. For longer retirements, many FIRE practitioners use 3 to 3.5 percent for added safety against sequence-of-returns risk.

faq.question: What are the different types of FIRE?
faq.answer: Lean FIRE targets minimal expenses below 40,000 per year. Fat FIRE aims for a comfortable lifestyle over 100,000 annually. Barista FIRE covers most expenses through investments but supplements with part-time work for extras and health insurance.
